# Cases for the comparison between the C GTS library and gts-cxx.
#
# Each line is: NAME  COMMAND ARGS...
# run-ref.sh replaces @DATA@ with test/data and @OUT@ with the output
# directory, so that a case can read the surface written by an earlier case.
# @NEW@ is the output directory too, for a file the case writes.
# @REF@ is gts-ref's output directory: there both programs read the surface
# the C library wrote.
# The boolean cases are generated by run-ref.sh from
# test/data/gts-boolean/tests and are not listed here.

# Generated spheres
sphere-0            sphere 0
sphere-1            sphere 1
sphere-2            sphere 2
sphere-3            sphere 3
sphere-4            sphere 4
sphere-5            sphere 5

# Iso-surfaces: 4 algorithms x 3 fields, 40 cells per axis; seeded is
# gts-cxx's marching cubes from a seed, and GTS's full marching cubes in C
iso-cartesian-sphere       iso cartesian sphere 40
iso-cartesian-torus        iso cartesian torus 40
iso-cartesian-blobs        iso cartesian blobs 40
iso-seeded-sphere          iso seeded sphere 40
iso-seeded-torus           iso seeded torus 40
iso-seeded-blobs           iso seeded blobs 40
iso-tetra-sphere           iso tetra sphere 40
iso-tetra-torus            iso tetra torus 40
iso-tetra-blobs            iso tetra blobs 40
iso-tetra_bounded-sphere   iso tetra_bounded sphere 40
iso-tetra_bounded-torus    iso tetra_bounded torus 40
iso-tetra_bounded-blobs    iso tetra_bounded blobs 40
iso-tetra_bcl-sphere       iso tetra_bcl sphere 40
iso-tetra_bcl-torus        iso tetra_bcl torus 40
iso-tetra_bcl-blobs        iso tetra_bcl blobs 40

# Marching cubes through the slice API, on the grid above with each point
# moved, so that it is not cartesian
isoslice-sphere            isoslice sphere 30
isoslice-torus             isoslice torus 30
isoslice-blobs             isoslice blobs 30

# Tessellation
tessellate-cube-2          tessellate @DATA@/gts-boolean/cube 2
tessellate-cube-2-mid      tessellate @DATA@/gts-boolean/cube 2 mid
tessellate-horse4-1        tessellate @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse4.gts 1

# Coarsening, with the cost and stop options of GTSRetriangulator
coarsen-horse5-length-number-300          coarsen @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts length number 300
coarsen-horse5-length-cost-0.01           coarsen @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts length cost 0.01
coarsen-horse5-volume-number-300          coarsen @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts volume number 300
coarsen-horse5-volume-number-300-mid      coarsen @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts volume number 300 mid
coarsen-horse5-angle-cost-0.4             coarsen @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts angle cost 0.4
coarsen-cylinder-volume-number-500        coarsen @DATA@/gts-boolean/1.gts volume number 500
coarsen-sphere5-volume-number-1000        coarsen @OUT@/sphere-5.gts volume number 1000
coarsen-iso-torus-length-cost-0.0625      coarsen @OUT@/iso-cartesian-torus.gts length cost 0.0625
coarsen-iso-torus-length-then-angle       coarsen @OUT@/coarsen-iso-torus-length-cost-0.0625.gts angle cost 0.4

# Refinement
refine-cube-length-number-200             refine @DATA@/gts-boolean/cube length number 200
refine-horse4-length-number-1500          refine @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse4.gts length number 1500
refine-horse4-length-cost-0.005           refine @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse4.gts length cost 0.005

# Cluster grid (out-of-core simplification)
cluster-horse5-0.005       cluster @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts 0.005
cluster-sphere5-0.1        cluster @OUT@/sphere-5.gts 0.1
cluster-cylinder-1         cluster @DATA@/gts-boolean/1.gts 1

# Distance between surfaces
distance-sphere4-sphere5   distance @OUT@/sphere-4.gts @OUT@/sphere-5.gts
distance-horse4-horse5     distance @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse4.gts @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts
distance-torus-bounded     distance @REF@/iso-tetra_bounded-torus.gts @REF@/iso-cartesian-torus.gts 0.05
distance-torus-coarse      distance @REF@/coarsen-iso-torus-length-cost-0.0625.gts @REF@/iso-cartesian-torus.gts

# Curvature at each vertex, by coordinates
curvature-sphere4          curvature @REF@/sphere-4.gts
curvature-horse5           curvature @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts
curvature-horse5-coarse    curvature @REF@/coarsen-horse5-volume-number-300.gts
curvature-torus            curvature @REF@/iso-cartesian-torus.gts
curvature-torus-bounded    curvature @REF@/iso-tetra_bounded-torus.gts
curvature-cube             curvature @DATA@/gts-boolean/cube

# Inside test, distance and closest point on a grid of points
inside-sphere4-9           inside @REF@/sphere-4.gts 9
inside-horse5-12           inside @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts 12
inside-torus-12            inside @REF@/iso-cartesian-torus.gts 12
inside-cube-8              inside @DATA@/gts-boolean/cube 8
inside-cube-9              inside @DATA@/gts-boolean/cube 9

# Faces on vertices of their own, merged back
merge-sphere4-0            merge @REF@/sphere-4.gts 0
merge-horse5-0             merge @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts 0
merge-horse5-1e-9          merge @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts 1e-9
merge-cube-0               merge @DATA@/gts-boolean/cube 0
merge-tetra-dup-0          merge @DATA@/tetra-dup.gts 0

# Centres of mass and area, boundary
centers-sphere4            centers @REF@/sphere-4.gts
centers-horse5             centers @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts
centers-torus-bounded      centers @REF@/iso-tetra_bounded-torus.gts

# Delaunay triangulation, as GTS's example delaunay.c: the points, then the
# constraints, then the options. The inputs are in test/data/delaunay.
delaunay-random-100                 delaunay @DATA@/delaunay/random-100.gts
delaunay-random-2000                delaunay @DATA@/delaunay/random-2000.gts
delaunay-cartesian-10               delaunay @DATA@/delaunay/cartesian-10.gts
delaunay-squarehole                 delaunay @DATA@/delaunay/squarehole.gts
delaunay-squarehole-holes           delaunay @DATA@/delaunay/squarehole.gts nohull holes
delaunay-two_segments               delaunay @DATA@/delaunay/two_segments.gts
delaunay-two_segments-noconst       delaunay @DATA@/delaunay/two_segments.gts noconst
delaunay-too_close-conform          delaunay @DATA@/delaunay/too_close.gts conform
delaunay-ring                       delaunay @DATA@/delaunay/ring.gts
delaunay-ring-holes                 delaunay @DATA@/delaunay/ring.gts nohull holes
delaunay-crossing                   delaunay @DATA@/delaunay/crossing.gts
delaunay-crossing-conform           delaunay @DATA@/delaunay/crossing.gts conform
delaunay-ring-conform-steiner-5     delaunay @DATA@/delaunay/ring.gts nohull holes conform steiner=5
delaunay-ring-quality-0.5           delaunay @DATA@/delaunay/ring.gts quality=0.5
delaunay-ring-holes-quality-0.6     delaunay @DATA@/delaunay/ring.gts nohull holes quality=0.6
delaunay-ring-holes-area-0.005      delaunay @DATA@/delaunay/ring.gts nohull holes quality=0.6 area=0.005
delaunay-squarehole-area-0.002      delaunay @DATA@/delaunay/squarehole.gts nohull holes quality=0.6 area=0.002
delaunay-two_segments-quality-0.5   delaunay @DATA@/delaunay/two_segments.gts quality=0.5
delaunay-crossing-quality-0.5       delaunay @DATA@/delaunay/crossing.gts quality=0.5 steiner=200

# Triangle strips
strip-horse5                        strip @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts
strip-sphere4                       strip @REF@/sphere-4.gts
strip-torus                         strip @REF@/iso-cartesian-torus.gts
strip-cylinder                      strip @DATA@/gts-boolean/1.gts
strip-cube                          strip @DATA@/gts-boolean/cube

# Progressive surfaces: the levels, then the finest level, which must be the
# input; written by each library, and the C library's file read by both.
psurface-horse5-300                 psurface @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts 300 200 400 600
psurface-sphere4-100                psurface @REF@/sphere-4.gts 100 100 300 500
psurface-delaunay-1000              psurface @REF@/delaunay-random-2000.gts 1000 500 1500
psurface-write-horse5               psurface-write @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts 300 @NEW@/psurface-horse5.psurf
psurface-write-delaunay             psurface-write @REF@/delaunay-random-2000.gts 1000 @NEW@/psurface-delaunay.psurf
psurface-read-horse5                psurface-read @REF@/psurface-horse5.psurf 200 400
psurface-read-delaunay              psurface-read @REF@/psurface-delaunay.psurf 500 1500

# Hierarchical surfaces, keyed by the x of each split's vertex: from the
# coarsest level, N expansions, N/2 collapses, then all expanded
hsurface-horse5-150                 hsurface @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts 300 150
hsurface-horse5-450                 hsurface @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts 300 450
hsurface-delaunay-800               hsurface @REF@/delaunay-random-2000.gts 1000 800

# The dual graph of a surface, and its partitions. GTS's reader of graphs in
# the Jostle format loops for ever on any graph with an edge, so the case is
# in the unit tests instead.
graph-horse5-stats                  graph @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts stats
graph-horse5-bubble-8               graph @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts bubble 8 10
graph-horse5-ggg                    graph @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts bisect ggg 10
graph-horse5-bfgg-kl                graph @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts bisect bfgg 10 kl 50
graph-horse5-ggg-bkl                graph @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts bisect ggg 10 bkl 50
graph-horse5-recursive-3            graph @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts recursive 3
graph-sphere4-recursive-2           graph @REF@/sphere-4.gts recursive 2
graph-horse5-pgraph-100             graph @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts pgraph 100
graph-horse5-io                     graph @DATA@/gts-boolean/horse5.gts io

# Height fields, as GTS's example happrox.c: a grid of heights from a PGM
# file, or scattered points (.xyz, as happrox -f), approximated by greedy
# insertion. The inputs are in test/data/happrox.
happrox-terrain-300                 happrox @DATA@/happrox/terrain-120x90.pgm number=300
happrox-terrain-3000                happrox @DATA@/happrox/terrain-120x90.pgm number=3000
happrox-terrain-cost-200            happrox @DATA@/happrox/terrain-120x90.pgm cost=200
happrox-terrain-relative            happrox @DATA@/happrox/terrain-120x90.pgm number=500 relative=5000
happrox-terrain8-200                happrox @DATA@/happrox/terrain8-64x48.pgm number=200
happrox-terrain8-cost-2             happrox @DATA@/happrox/terrain8-64x48.pgm cost=2
happrox-points-300                  happrox @DATA@/happrox/points-2000.xyz number=300
happrox-points-keep-300             happrox @DATA@/happrox/points-2000.xyz number=300 keep
happrox-points-closed-cost-0.02     happrox @DATA@/happrox/points-2000.xyz cost=0.02 closed
happrox-points-relative             happrox @DATA@/happrox/points-2000.xyz number=400 relative=0.5
